sound_design.note: Sound effects synthesised in the project (pipeline/sound.py): a stone part set in place. Levels are relative to the narration's peak; the whole mix is then loudness-normalised. An agent cannot listen: the owner decides whether they help.

with_sfx.text: Our first platform in this illustrative design carries four blocks of three-story homes. Altogether, it weighs about 4,800 tons and floats about three meters deep. And here's the surprise, more than half of that weight is the concrete hull itself.

_no_sfx.text: Our first platform in this illustrative design carries four blocks of three-story homes. Altogether, it weighs about 4,800 tons and floats about three meters deep. And here's the surprise, more than half of that weight is the concrete hull itself.

with_sfx.text: Now add a fourth story. The platform settles about a third of a meter deeper, and the freeboard, the part of the hull above the water, shrinks from about a meter to about 70 centimeters.

_no_sfx.text: Now add a fourth story. The platform settles about a third of a meter deeper, and the freeboard, the part of the hull above the water, shrinks from about a meter to about 70 centimeters.

with_sfx.text: One fix is to make the hull half a meter deeper. That adds about 100 tons of concrete, 4% more, and brings the freeboard back to about a meter and 15 centimeters. Lighter buildings would be another way.

_no_sfx.text: One fix is to make the hull half a meter deeper. That adds about 100 tons of concrete, 4% more, and brings the freeboard back to about a meter and 15 centimeters. Lighter buildings would be another way.

with_sfx.text: Will it tip over? Move 100 tons out toward the edge, and in this example the platform tilts by less than half a degree. But a small tilt under a shifted load tells us very little about how it will move in waves. Floating is only the first problem.
